gate: Speaker B identity across the whole rendered set, before anything is tokenised.

render.renderer: tools/synthesize_turns.py, one long-lived runtime, 19-26 s per turn on mps

measurement.sampling_note: 160 clips give 12,720 pairs; 4,000 were sampled with a recorded seed, which is ample for a 5th percentile.

gates.fixed_in: m3/DATASET_SPEC.md, before any turn was rendered

interpretation: The worst pair in 4,000 scores 0.6542, which is close to the MEAN a single real human produces (0.6983) under the same pipeline. Channel B is one speaker by a wide margin, and at 0.0767 against the target speaker it is unambiguously a different person.
limits: ECAPA similarity says these clips come from one voice; it does not say the voice is pleasant or the reading correct. Intelligibility of channel B is not gated here, and B never appears in the held-out evaluation.
